content: We have search results with three templates. Need to return the mapped_rxn associated with the template that, when applied to the molecule, reproduces the reaction: DIBAL-H reduction of ester to aldehyde? Actually description: DIBAL-H reduces esters and nitriles to aldehydes. Reaction: carbon-oxygen bond broken, another carbon-oxygen bond order changes from 2 to 1, forming aliphatic hydroxyls functional group. So forward reaction: ester -> aldehyde? Wait DIBAL-H reduces ester to aldehyde, not to alcohol. But description says forming aliphatic hydroxyls functional group. That seems contradictory. Maybe they refer to reduction of ester to aldehyde then further to alcohol? Actually DIBAL-H reduces ester to aldehyde, which has carbonyl (C=O) and an OH? Aldehyde functional group is carbonyl with H, not hydroxyl. But they say forming aliphatic hydroxyls. Could be reduction of ester to primary alcohol? DIBAL-H can reduce nitrile to aldehyde, not to alcohol. But maybe they consider the forward reaction as breaking C-O bond (ester) and forming C-O single bond (alcohol). So product is alcohol. So we need template that transforms ester to alcohol (i.e., reduction). The search used functional_groups_broken carboxylic esters, formed aliphatic hydroxyls. The results include three templates. Need to pick the one that when applied to our molecule (the target) reproduces the reaction. The target molecule is given in previous step: from make_5_lvl2-apply_template-2 answer: precursors list: ['C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO', 'COP(=O)(CC(=O)O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)OC'] That's the result of applying some template to the molecule? Actually that answer gave precursors of applying the template from previous task. Now we need to find the template that when applied to the molecule (the original target?) reproduces the reaction. The molecule we have is likely the product of DIBAL-H reduction? The given molecule in input is the product? The SMILES: C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO. This looks like a cyclic acetal? Contains an aldehyde? It has C=O at end? Actually ...C=O inside? There's C=O in side chain: C/C=C/C=O (an aldehyde). The molecule also has a primary alcohol at end (CO). So maybe the target is a molecule with an aldehyde that could be reduced to alcohol? The template should break carbonyl (C=O) of aldehyde to alcohol? But functional groups broken: aldehydes? The earlier attempt used aldehydes but invalid. Should use "aldehydes" functional group (plural). Let's try search with broken aldehydes, formed aliphatic hydroxyls.
